where.test: R1 R2 R4 R5 R9: the stepsWorld fixture drives the real steps for a run it holds, refuses the rest by their codes, and records every act
R1: a machine credential creates a step only for a run it holds, doer system with that run's enabled_by
R1: stepCreate records a step at planned, answering {ok, step, place, at}; the refusals in order, each writing nothing
R10: learned is a member's own words, at most 2,000 characters, revisable by its writer with history; a machine writes none
R11: a loop is refused STEP_WAIT_CYCLE naming the path; a wait on a step seen more narrowly STEP_WAIT_NARROWER
R11: a step with an unmet wait reads waiting, naming each; stepStart refused STEP_WAITING; a step wait met when that step ends or is set aside, the read saying which
R11: arrivals are answered by registered sources; one nobody can read is undetermined, never met

R12 (T46): stepsDue reads at most 1,000 of her dated steps not ended, in step order, and at most 1,000 of her reminders due by that day, in the order she asked them; past either bound the answer carries truncated: true beside due, otherwise no truncated (controls: 1,000 exactly, an ended step, a reminder not yet due, another member's)
R12: byWhen is {date, basis, source?}; nearing within 7 local days changes nothing else; stepsDue answers only the member who set the date, keyed; stepReminder on its day to her alone
R13: stepCostAdd appends a fee or purchase in an exact decimal, with who and when; stepCostRemove by its writer only, recorded
R14: costShares answers a costed step's totals and sharing projects to each owner of each, when two or more draw and none is hidden; else nothing to anyone
R15: costMessage by an owner of a sharing project relays her text once to the owners of each other one; costMessages answers it with the writer's handle and no project
R16: questionFollow records a member's own choice on a question she may see, answered to her alone; nothing names, lists or counts followers
R17: findRecipients: joined participants of every drawing project, less who stopped, plus who chose to follow, each while she may see the question; bounded and paged
R18: the step authority resolver shows a look's row exactly to whoever sees the step; promotion refuses a leg on a step as STEP_NOT_A_LEG inside BASIS_REFUSED
R19: steps, learned lines, costs and messages are working material: no table is exported to the public, and no figure is made from them
R19: steps, learned lines, costs and messages are working material: no table is exported to the public, and no figure is made from them > <name not written out, line 16>
R2: who sees a step: question-placed through a referring question, project-placed at FULL sight, group-placed every active member; any other as absent
R20: nothing measures a member: no answer counts steps, outcomes or costs per member; every act has a member's path that needs no AI
R20: nothing measures a member: no answer counts steps, outcomes or costs per member; every act has a member's path that needs no AI > <name not written out, line 47>
R21: a step holds no step: no place names a step, and nothing nests one step in another
R22: tables declared through record-core.declareTable; project steps purged with their project, question steps with their last question, group steps with the store; follows owner-sighted

R23 (T44): a store holding later_found entries from before looked_at gains the column at start, each entry filled from its look's own row; one whose look the log no longer holds answers null, never the arrival's instant

R23 (T44): each later_found entry answers looked_at, the instant of the look (its observation-log entry's at), beside at, the instant what arrived was logged (negative control: the two differ, and looked_at is the look's, not the arrival's)

R23 (T47): laterFound answers {ok, found, truncated}, reading at most LATER_FOUND_SCAN (5,000) entries oldest first, before any is filtered by at, sight or recipient; truncated: 5,001 entries answer truncated: true (control: 5,000 answer false); a viewer naming no member, or a read that fails, answers found [] and truncated false
R23: a PRESENT at a subject a step's look found absent gives the step a later_found entry; the look is unchanged; laterFound tells each recipient and the doer once, keyed

R23: laterFound's `at` is compared as an instant, never as a string (an entry logged in the same second as `at`, spelled with milliseconds, is told); a read past LATER_FOUND_SCAN entries says truncated

R24, R6: a decided proposal never names a step that has gone — deleting the step it created clears the proposal's step, and a store holding such a name is cleared at start (negative control: a proposal whose step is held still names it)
R24: stepAccept, a member's act, in one of record-grammar R52's forms, recording which and who; a set-aside proposal stays readable with her reason
R24: stepPropose holds a machine's proposal apart, labelled the system's, never a step until accepted
R26: acceptanceCounts answers, group-wide only, how many were accepted in each form, naming no member, project or proposal; registered with record-core's counts
R27: nothing here reads the project's bar or gates a step by it
R28: stepAccept refuses a proposed step that is absent or unseen with NO_SUCH_STEP_PROPOSAL (C-142.28, its number and translation unchanged), never NO_SUCH_PROPOSAL (intent's)
R29: a holder that throws or answers anything but {entry} is read as not held, so the step's own item stays

R29: fn is asked {step, byWhen, waits} for a step with a date; a held step draws no past-date item from stepsDue, and every read answers by_when_held {module, entry} beside byWhen (null when not held); her own reminder stays
R29: registerDueHolder takes one holder, once, through membership.listenerRefusal: a second is LISTENER_DECLARED naming the holder, a malformed one LISTENER_MALFORMED, each registering nothing
R29: the control: with no holder registered, stepsDue answers as R12 does today, and every read answers by_when_held null
R3: a question-placed step names its doer by handle, and its project only while not hidden; hidden and none answer alike
